cards.explanation: The answer is the land itself. God says, “…the land itself must observe a Sabbath to the LORD.” Not just the people. Verse 4 says the seventh year is “…a Sabbath of complete rest for the land…” and that's a whole year off. I know folks who can't rest half as well as a field can.

The answer is False. In the Sabbath year, God says, “You are not to reap the aftergrowth of your harvest or gather the grapes of your untended vines.” The land must have a year of complete rest. So the vines get left alone, friends, and that's the whole point.

The answer is the household and even the wild animals. The food is for you, your manservant and maidservant, the hired hand or foreigner who stays with you, your livestock and the wild animals in your land. That's a wide table, friends. Even the critters get a seat, and they didn't have to bring a dish.

The answer is the Day of Atonement. God says to sound the horn “…on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement.” (Leviticus 25:9) Seven times seven years, forty-nine of them, and then THE HORN. I think that's the loudest alarm clock anybody ever got, and nobody's hitting snooze on it. It goes “…far and wide…” and it's the signal for the fiftieth year, the Jubilee.

The answer is back to his own property and clan. God says, “…each of you is to return to his property and to his clan.” Then verse 13 says it again, that each shall return to his own property. Liberty means going home, friends.

The answer is True. God says, “The fiftieth year will be a Jubilee for you; you are not to sow the land or reap its aftergrowth or harvest the untended vines.” (Leviticus 25:11) So the land rests in the seventh year and rests again in the fiftieth. Plenty of time to put its feet up.

The answer is higher for more years left, and lower for fewer years left. More years before the Jubilee means more harvests to sell, so God says you “…shall increase the price in proportion to a greater number of years…” It's like a big batch of cookies costing more than a half dozen. Fewer years left means fewer harvests, so God says to “…decrease it in proportion to a lesser number of years…” Then He gives the reason: “for he is selling you a given number of harvests.”

The answer is that they will dwell securely in the land. God says to keep His statutes and carefully observe His judgments “…so that you may dwell securely in the land.” Verse 19 adds that they can eat their fill and dwell in safety. Security and a full belly, friends, that's what He says follows.

The answer is that the land yields a crop for three years. God says, “But I will send My blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that the land will yield a crop sufficient for three years.” That answers the worry about what they'd eat in the seventh year. God answers their question before they even have to ask it twice.

The answer is that the land belongs to the LORD. That's the heart of it, friends. God says, “The land must not be sold permanently, because it is Mine, and you are but foreigners and residents with Me.” It's His land, so nobody sells it for good.

The answer is his nearest of kin. God says, “…his nearest of kin may come and redeem what his brother has sold.” Notice the word may, so the door is open for a close relative to step in. Having someone like that around is a gift.

The answer is years. God says, “…he shall calculate the years since its sale, repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.” It's a count of years, and then home he goes. Years are what this whole chapter counts, from the Sabbath year to the Jubilee.

The answer is False. If he can't get enough to repay, the land stays with the buyer only until the Year of Jubilee. Then God says, “In the Jubilee, however, it is to be released, so that he may return to his property.” So the sale has an end date built in, friends.

The answer is to help him so he can keep living among them. God says to help him “…as you would a foreigner or stranger, so that he can continue to live among you.” (Leviticus 25:35) The goal is that he keeps living right there with his people. I think that means the help is meant to come while he's still standing in the neighborhood, not after. The command is simple: help him.

The answer is any interest or profit. God says, “Do not take any interest or profit from him, but fear your God, that your countryman may live among you.” No interest, no profit. The goal is that he can keep living among them.

The answer is as a hired worker and not a slave. God says, “…you must not force him into slave labor.” Instead he stays “…as a hired worker or temporary resident…” and works for the buyer until the Year of Jubilee. That's a hired worker's arrangement, friends, not a slave's.

The answer is True. God says, “Then he and his children are to be released, and he may return to his clan and to the property of his fathers.” The Year of Jubilee frees the man and his children. And the way back to his clan and his fathers' property is open to him.

The answer is that they're His servants He brought out of Egypt. God says, “Because the Israelites are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt, they are not to be sold as slaves.” Their belonging starts with Him. Verse 55 says it again: “For the Israelites are My servants.”

The answer is False. God says, “…as for your brothers, the Israelites, no man may rule harshly over his brother.” (Leviticus 25:46) He says the same in verse 43: “You are not to rule over them harshly, but you shall fear your God.” So under these rules, harshness toward a fellow Israelite is ruled out in both places.

The answer is bought. The word in the text is redeem, and here it means someone pays the price to buy him back. God says one of his brothers may redeem him, and then lists his uncle, his cousin or any close relative from his clan. If he prospers, he may even redeem himself.

The answer is False. Even if nobody buys him back, God says, “…he and his children shall be released in the Year of Jubilee.” (Leviticus 25:54) The Jubilee frees him, and his children go free with him. Redemption is one way out, friends, and the Jubilee is there even without it.
